details:
🪐 Marswalk Navigator — Plan. Explore. Return.

Marswalk Navigator is an AI-powered Mars exploration and mission-planning platform designed to help future astronauts explore the Martian surface more safely, efficiently, and scientifically.

🧭 What Does Our Project Do?

Our application combines interactive Mars mapping, terrain visualization, intelligent route planning, and simulated environmental monitoring into one unified platform. Users can explore Mars through 2D orbital maps and interactive 3D visualizations, select destinations, compare routes, analyze terrain conditions, and plan simulated astronaut surface missions.

A major innovation is MARA (Mars Adaptive Risk Assistant), an AI-assisted mission companion that helps users understand potential route hazards, compare exploration strategies, evaluate simulated resource limitations, and make informed mission-planning decisions.

The platform integrates NASA Mars Trek archival imagery and planetary data sources while clearly distinguishing authentic scientific information from simulated terrain and environmental conditions.

🎯 How Does It Address the Challenge?

Future Mars missions will require astronauts to navigate unfamiliar terrain while managing limited resources and identifying valuable scientific exploration opportunities.

Marswalk Navigator addresses this challenge by bringing mapping, route analysis, scientific exploration, and mission planning together into a single interactive workspace.

Our route-planning system uses the A algorithm* to calculate and compare alternative paths based on modeled terrain risks and scientific priorities.

🛠️ Technologies and Tools Used

We developed Marswalk Navigator using:

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, HTML, and CSS.
  • 3D Visualization: Three.js and React Three Fiber.
  • Backend: Node.js and Express.js.
  • Database: MongoDB for mission history, observations, and assistant conversations.
  • AI Integration: MARA, featuring rule-based assistance and optional language-model integration.
  • Scientific Data: NASA Mars Trek orbital mapping services and documented planetary datasets.
  • UI/UX: Lovable-assisted design and custom interactive dashboard components.
  • Development: JavaScript, TypeScript, GitHub, and modern web-development tools.

The application is designed to run on standard computers without requiring specialized hardware.

💡 What Makes Our Project Creative?

Our innovation lies in combining AI-assisted decision-making, planetary mapping, interactive 3D exploration, and scientific mission planning into a single educational platform.

Instead of simply displaying images of Mars, Marswalk Navigator allows users to interact with planetary information, examine possible exploration routes, and understand the trade-offs between scientific discovery and mission constraints.

MARA further enhances the experience by providing an interactive assistant that connects mission-related questions with the application's available planning tools.

🌍 Benefits and Intended Impact

Marswalk Navigator aims to make planetary exploration more accessible to students, researchers, space enthusiasts, and future mission planners.

It demonstrates how artificial intelligence, geospatial technologies, and data-driven analysis could contribute to safer and more productive exploration beyond Earth.

During development, we considered scientific accuracy, user accessibility, mission constraints, performance, realistic data representation, and the importance of clearly identifying simulated information.

Although Marswalk Navigator is an educational simulator rather than a flight-certified navigation system, it provides a foundation for exploring how integrated digital tools could support future astronaut missions.

🌟 Our Vision

We believe the future of space exploration depends not only on reaching new worlds but also on making intelligent decisions once we arrive.

Marswalk Navigator represents our effort to bring that vision closer to reality.

Explore Beyond Boundaries. Navigate with Intelligence. Return with Discovery. 🌠
